sentences.text: The present application under Section 439 (2) of Cr.P.C. has been filed for cancellation of bail granted to the respondent no.2 by the learned Trial Court vide order dated 28.1.2025 passed in Bail Application No.254/2025.

Brief facts for disposal of the case are that an FIR bearing Crime No.427/2022 was registered against the respondent no.2 for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 409 of IPC Respondent no.2 filed an application for grant of anticipatory bail vide Bail Application No.254/2025 and was granted bail by the Trial Court vide order dated 28.1.2025.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18067 2 MCRC-12990-2025

Learned counsel for the applicant has argued before this Court that the learned Trial Court by impugned order had not considered certain material facts and as such had erred in passing the impugned order granting anticipatory bail to the present respondent no.2 and in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Jayaben Vs. Tejas Kanubhai Zala and Another reported in 2022(1) Crimes 207 (SC)

sentences.text: the order of grant of anticipatory bail to the present respondent is not sustainable and it was further argued that once it is found that the order releasing the accused on bail is unsustainable as a necessary consequence shall have to follow and bail has to be cancelled.

Learned counsel has further argued that so far as merits of the matter is concerned the present respondent have taken Rs.36 Lakhs for providing certain machineries, but the machineries which were provided to the present applicant were defective and when the matter was complained to the respondents that he further asked a sum of Rs.3 Lakhs, but thereafter neither supplied any machinery nor had returned the amount and even the machineries were not called back, but this aspect was not considered by the learned Trial Court while granting bail and as on date neither the machinery has been provided to the present applicant nor the amount has been recovered from the respondents.
Thus, it was prayed that the anticipatory bail granted in favour of the respondent no.2 be recalled.

On the other hand Shri M.P.S. Raghuvanshi, learned Senior Counsel for the respondent no.2 by placing reliance in the matter of Deepak Yadav Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another, (2022) 8 SCC 559 had argued that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18067 3 MCRC-12990-2025 there is no doubt true that cancellation of bail cannot be limited to the occurrence of supervening circumstances and the Court certainly has the inherent powers and discretion to cancel the bail of an accused even in the absence of supervening circumstances.

entities.text: Deepak Yadav Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another, (2022) 8 SCC 559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The learned Apex Court while enumerating the instances on which bail can be cancelled in para 33 had given illustrative circumstances where the bail can be cancelled and as the case of present applicant has not fall within the aforesaid parameters or the instances given by the Apex Court, the present M.Cr.C.
deserves to be dismissed.

Learned counsel has further submitted that under the agreement between the parties dated 25.5.2019 there is a dispute resolution mechanism provided, but without availing the dispute resolution mechanism the present applicant has choose to make a complaint and as the very nature of the complaint is of civil nature, the learned Trial Court has rightly allowed the application for anticipatory bail which in absence of any material should not be tinkered lightly.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of the present application.
Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
After perusing the case diary as well as record, this Court finds that there is no strength in the arguments as advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.

The Apex Court in the matter of Deepak Yadav (supra) in para 31 to 33 has observed with regard to cancellation of bail as under:
31.

This Court has reiterated in several instances that bail once NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18067 4 MCRC-12990-2025 granted, should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying the concession of bail during trial.

sentences.text: Having said that, in case of cancellation of bail, very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing cancellation of bail (which was already granted).

32. A two-Judge Bench of this Court in Dolat Ram And Others Vs. State of Haryana 17 laid down the grounds for cancellation of bail which are :-
(i) interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of Justice (ii) evasion or attempt to evade the due course of justice (iii) abuse of the concession granted to the accused in any manner (iv) Possibility of accused absconding (v) Likelihood of/actual misuse of bail (vi) Likelihood of the accused tampering with the evidence or threatening witnesses.
33.

entities.text: Dolat Ram And Others Vs. State of Haryana 17
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is no doubt true that cancellation of bail cannot be limited to the occurrence of supervening circumstances.
This Court certainly has the inherent powers and discretion to cancel the bail of an accused even in the absence of supervening circumstances.

Following are the illustrative circumstances where the bail can be cancelled :-
a) Where the court granting bail takes into account irrelevant material of substantial nature and not trivial nature while ignoring relevant material on record.

b) Where the court granting bail overlooks the influential position of the accused in comparison to the victim of abuse or the witnesses especially when there is prima facie misuse of position and power over the victim.
c) Where the past criminal record and conduct of the accused is completely ignored while granting bail.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18067 5 MCRC-12990-2025 d) Where bail has been granted on untenable grounds.
e) Where serious discrepancies are found in the order granting bail thereby causing prejudice to justice.
f) Where the grant of bail was not appropriate in the first place given the very serious nature of the charges against the accused which disentitles him for bail and thus cannot be justified.

sentences.text: When the order granting bail is apparently whimsical, capricious and perverse in the facts of the given case.

This Court after going through the impugned order finds that none of the eventuality as has been enumerated by the Apex Court in the aforesaid matter is made out as the very ground in challenge the application for cancellation of anticipatory bail is that there was no proper appreciation of the material available on record.

According to this Court the aforesaid ground does not meet the criteria of cancellation of bail as has been held by the Apex Court the bail can be cancelled if te Courts takes into account irrelevant material of substantial nature and not trivial nature while ignoring relevant material on record, where the past criminal record and conduct of the accused is completely ignored or bail has been granted only on untenable grounds or there are serious discrepancies in the order granting bail thereby causing prejudice to justice or the order granting bail is apparently whimsical,
capricious and perverse the bail can be cancelled, but as none of the eventuality therein there is no reason to interfere with the said order.
Accordingly, the present petition is hereby dismissed. .

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18067 6 MCRC-12990-2025 JUDGE (aspr)
